note: Five seeded case studies (one per area + one cross-area). Gold conflicts are tension types from rules.TENSIONS; expected SDLC models and gold documents are hand-labelled by the author. Retrieval questions are phrased the way a stakeholder would ask, without document names.

cases.name: Hyderabad GPU campus, 40 MW
cases.brief: We are building a 40 MW GPU campus near Hyderabad for enterprise tenants. Power comes from the Telangana DISCOM plus a solar PPA. We need to report both location and market Scope 2 for the BRSR Core filing. Tenants may process personal data. We must follow CERT-In incident rules and keep PUE low while riding through grid events.

cases.name: DISCOM smart-meter analytics
cases.brief: A state distribution company wants an analytics platform over 2 million smart meters: 15-minute interval reads, outage detection, theft alerts and demand-response forecasts. Releases every two weeks. Data sits in a government cloud and integrates with the billing system through open APIs. Consumer names and addresses are personal data under the DPDP Act. The platform must meet CEA AMI functional requirements and RDSS reporting.

cases.name: Scope 2 report for a cloud tenant
cases.brief: A listed IT services company rents racks in three colocation data centres and needs a Scope 2 emissions report for its BRSR Core disclosure, with reasonable assurance. It buys renewable energy certificates for one site. The report must show location-based and market-based totals, the emission factors used and an audit trail that auditors can verify. Requirements are fixed by the regulator for this year.

cases.name: LLM procurement rules, state agency
cases.brief: A state agency will buy a large language model service for citizen helpdesks in three languages. It needs procurement rules: risk assessment before purchase, red-teaming for prompt injection, logging, human review of answers on benefits, data residency in India and a process to report AI incidents. Vendors may use third-party foundation models. The risks are new and not well understood.

cases.name: Grid-aware AI training scheduler
cases.brief: A cloud provider wants a scheduler that shifts AI training jobs to hours with low grid carbon intensity and responds to grid operator demand-response signals within 15 minutes. It must report the carbon saved for ESG disclosures, keep tenant SLAs, follow grid code limits and log every decision for audit. The scheduling logic will change often as tariffs change.
